name: Saudi Arabian Sign Language
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: sign language; published work (Morris & Schneider 2012; Altamimi & Alsager 2023) covers morphology/word order, no prosody description located

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Saudi Sign Language' (wikitext via API, 2026-09-17), reference list
sources.note: Used only as a bibliography lead: cites Morris & Schneider 2012, Sprenger & Mathur 2012, Altamimi & Alsager 2023, Kozak & Tomita 2012, Lamar University theses (Alamri 2017 x2, Alofi 2020: interpreter/teacher attitudes, life stories) and dictionary links (SignPuddle; Princess Alanood Foundation PDF now dead, returns HTML). No prosody source among them.

sources.citation: Altamimi, Haya S. & Haroon N. Alsager. 2023. Argument Structure and Word Order in Saudi Sign Language. Journal of Language Teaching and Research 14(1): 203-214. doi:10.17507/jltr.1401.21
sources.note: Full text read and a full-text search for stress/accent: no occurrence of stress/prosody/accent/intonation applied to SSL; only remarks that interrogatives carry nonmanual grammatical markers (raised eyebrows, forward/downward head movement) and that declaratives are produced 'without any additional nonmanual markings'; references to 'intonation breaks' concern ASL (Fischer 1975, Liddell 1980), not SSL. Syntax paper; silent on word stress.
sources.venue: Journal of Language Teaching and Research

sources.citation: Morris, Carla & Erin Schneider. 2012. On Selected Morphemes in Saudi Arabian Sign Language. Sign Language Studies 13(1): 103-121.

sources.note: Self-described part of a grammatical sketch; covers nonmanual intensifiers ('intense face', tongue movements) which is the nearest thing to prosodic/prominence marking described for the language.
